A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EasyRec and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendix A. All 12 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot recommendation experiments, collaborative-filtering comparisons, training-objective and profile-diversification analyses, and a preference-shift case study in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the recommendation scores in Tables 3–5 and analyses in Figures 4–5.

M1.justification: Collaborative profiling, the Transformer embedder, contrastive and masked-language-model losses, profile diversification, and cosine-similarity ranking remain unchanged. The preference-score wording does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train on the same six Amazon categories and evaluate on Sports, Steam, and Yelp, retaining the same recommendation tasks and preference-shift scenario. Swapping the Games/Movies statistics labels does not change domain coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 5 retain the same language-model comparators and GCCF/LightGCN comparisons. Appendix A.3 retains their settings; the added Self-Instruct citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Table 1 swaps the statistics assigned to Movies and Games. Movies changes from 17,397 users, 8,330 items, and 120,255 interactions to 16,994 users, 9,370 items, and 134,649 interactions, with the reverse for Games. This revises reported dataset sizes; preprocessing, splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged, and no experimental rerun is established.

E4.justification: The BPR-versus-contrastive comparison in Table 4, model-size analysis, diversification-count analysis in Figure 4, and preference-shift case study in Figure 5 are unchanged. The appendix adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Table 3's p < 0.05 significance notation, Table 5's five-run means, and Section 4.1.2's averaging across diversified profiles. No uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: Recommendation scores, ablation outcomes, plotted trends, case-study recommendations, and appendix cost figures are unchanged. For example, EasyRec-Large Recall@20 remains 0.0557 on Sports, 0.0225 on Steam, and 0.0065 on Yelp. Table 1's reassignment concerns dataset-size reporting rather than experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–14 remain unchanged, with no added proofs or formal assumptions. Replacing likelihood terminology with preference-score terminology does not revise the mathematical formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about zero-shot recommendation, collaborative alignment, scaling behavior, integration with existing recommenders, and adaptation to changing preferences.

C2.justification: Explanations attributing performance to collaborative signals and profile diversification, interpretations of scaling and preference adaptation, and applicability discussions remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or qualification is added.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same implementation details, hyperparameters, 25-epoch training, preprocessing instructions, profile-generation procedures, prompts, model checkpoints, and costs. Code and data access statements are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al.'s Self-Instruct reference and cites it alongside WizardLM in Section 3.3, replacing v1's duplicated WizardLM citation. The other 50 references match after renumbering, and the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 replaces interaction likelihood and likelihood value with preference-score terminology and lightly revises the surrounding sentence. Citation numbering and the arXiv version/date change, while the narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 exchanges the Games and Movies row labels without redesigning the table. The additional reference causes minor bibliography reflow; all figures and other table layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: The preference-score terminology more accurately describes cosine-similarity ranking, and replacing the duplicated WizardLM citation with Self-Instruct and WizardLM improves attribution. These are limited improvements in precision and documentation. The Games/Movies statistics are relabeled without establishing changed experiments, while the empirical evidence and appendix details remain unchanged.
